citations.title: Community-Integrated Living Arrangements Licensure and Certification Act
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for CILA agency licensure and site certification. A CILA is a site where 8 or fewer individuals with a developmental disability live under agency supervision.

citations.title: Licensure of community developmental services agencies
citations.requirement: Licensure requirements and fees. Application fee is capped at $200. Rule 115.410(b) points to Section 4(d) for the nonrefundable licensure and renewal fee. Agencies certify compliance with Section 4 in the application.

citations.title: Purpose
citations.requirement: Sets uniform direction for licensure and operation of CILA agencies.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines the terms the manual must use. Key definitions: CILA (8 or fewer), Continuous supervision or support (staff physically on-site all hours individuals are present unless the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy say otherwise), Critical Incidents, DSP, Implementation Strategy, Informed consent, Coercion, Aversive procedures, Restraint, Governing body, Authorized CILA agency representative, Independent Monitor and Receiver, Community integration, Authorized electronic monitoring.

citations.title: Description
citations.requirement: CILA settings and services must support integration and full community access, control of personal resources, privacy, dignity and respect, and freedom from coercion and restraint (except as 115.245 allows). They must optimize individual initiative and autonomy and be physically accessible, with communal areas meeting ADA standards. Agencies must follow person-centered planning rules (42 CFR 441.301(c)(1)-(3), 59 Ill. Adm. Code 120, 115.230). The CILA rate excludes day programs, which are billed separately. Informed consent to participate in a CILA must be documented. Subsection letters to be pinned from the official text.

citations.title: Respite Services for Persons with a Developmental Disability
citations.requirement: Before respite, the agency requires a physician statement that the individual has no contagious disease. It also documents that the individual will not jeopardize the health or safety of others in the home. Respite longer than two weeks needs Department approval before the initial two weeks end, and only in emergencies.

citations.title: Criteria for Participation of Individuals
citations.requirement: Individuals must be at least 18 with a developmental disability and need CILA services and a supervised living arrangement. Agencies may request an age waiver for individuals at least 17.5. An agency's lack of capacity for a particular disability does not make the individual ineligible. No otherwise qualified individual may be denied placement solely on diagnosis. Admission policies must be in writing and available for review (subsection to be pinned).

citations.title: Individuals Requiring Additional Services and Support
citations.requirement: Process for team requests for additional staff resources or supports. The Department responds as soon as possible and no later than ten business days after receipt. Need for non-base support hours is professionally reviewed at least annually and reported to the Department. Subsection letters to be pinned.

citations.title: Criteria for Termination from a CILA Agency
citations.requirement: Sets the criteria under which services may be terminated. 115.250 says individuals may remain in a CILA unless they voluntarily withdraw or meet these criteria. Section text was NOT retrieved; pull it verbatim before finalizing.

citations.title: Services and Supports
citations.requirement: The agency maintains a Provider Support Team for each individual. The team includes a QIDP and a DSP, plus a nurse or other professionals as needed. The team is responsible for service functions in the Personal Plan areas the agency covers and for developing the Implementation Strategy. It provides care and supervision based on assessed needs, helps the person take part in community supports, and is available 24 hours. It advocates, helps the person keep safety and comforts, and provides counseling and crisis problem-solving. It helps with ADLs and assistive devices and helps individuals access medication information, including observing and reporting effects and side effects. It supports the individual's right to sexual health and freedom from sexual exploitation, including a decision-making capacity assessment for consent to sexual activity.

citations.title: Assessments
citations.requirement: Individual assessments inform the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy. Rule text mentions an annual Department web-based health risk screening tool, with a paper-completion request allowed with justification. The section text and subsection number were NOT confirmed; verify before citing the subsection.

citations.title: Person-Centered Planning
citations.requirement: Agencies comply with 42 CFR 441.301(c)(1)-(3) and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 120. Within 20 calendar days of the provider's dated signature on the Personal Plan, the agency develops an Implementation Strategy on Form IL462-4470. The strategy is based on the Personal Plan and assessments, with the individual and guardian taking part (ISC as necessary). It is signed by the individual and guardian and addresses the outcomes the agency agreed to support. The individual and guardian get a copy of the strategy and its updates, and it becomes part of the record. At least monthly the QIDP reviews the strategy and documents the review. A CILA rate determination packet for intermittent supports is submitted by the ISC with the CILA agency. Individuals needing continuous supervision may stay alone or access the community independently only under specified circumstances. The provider support team must assess this, and it must be based on need and preference, not staff convenience. The strategy states the time periods and locations/time frames involved.

citations.title: Medical Services and Medications
citations.requirement: When agency employees provide medical services or medications, or supervise their administration, the agency certifies this is done under the Mental Health and DD Administrative Act and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116. A licensed physician (MD/DO) is responsible for medical services, including prescribing. A physician examines the individual before psychotropics start. AIMS screening is done at least every six months for individuals on psychotropics. A physician reviews medications and sees the individual at least every six months, more often if a psychiatrist requires.

citations.title: Restraints
citations.requirement: Prone, supine and mechanical restraint are prohibited. Any use must be reported in CIRAS and to the Office of the Inspector General. Other restraint is allowed only if every condition is met. There must be an immediate threat of serious physical harm, with less restrictive measures proven ineffective. Restraint must be a modification in the Personal Plan, approved by the individual or guardian and the Provider Support Team, and in the behavior strategy. It needs Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee approval and a plan to reduce and eliminate it. Staff must be trained in the specific restraint, and the agency must document no medical or psychological contraindication. Staff involved in restraint not in the Personal Plan may be required to complete remediation training. The agency keeps a copy of its restraint policy.

citations.title: Individual Rights and Confidentiality
citations.requirement: The agency shares and explains the current Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201) at entry and annually. Rights are protected under Chapter II of the Mental Health and DD Code, and seclusion is not permitted. Individuals have the right to remain in the CILA unless they withdraw or meet 115.215 criteria. They may contact the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, Equip for Equality, the Department's OIG, the Department and the agency's human rights committee. Staff offer help and give each individual the address and telephone number of GAC, OIG, the Department and Equip for Equality. Individuals have the right to be free from abuse, neglect, exploitation, coercion and restraint. Seclusion, time-out and aversive procedures are prohibited. Individuals may use private physicians and professionals of their choice, documented in the plan.

citations.title: Environmental Management of Living Arrangements
citations.requirement: Copies of local and State health, sanitation and environment inspections are maintained. The agency keeps a disaster preparedness plan covering disasters and public health crises, reviewed annually. Fire and disaster training records are available to DDD and BALC at the site, and corrective actions for drill or inspection deficiencies are recorded. Staff and individuals know how to react to fire, severe weather, missing persons, psychiatric and medical emergencies, poison control and deaths. Staff are trained in the location of extinguishers, first aid kits and evacuation routes. An operational telephone is accessible, with a posted list of the site phone number and nearest poison control center. Evacuation drills include actual evacuation to safe areas. At least one approved fire extinguisher has an annual inspection tag. Red Cross-standard first aid kits are checked quarterly and restocked. New individuals are trained within 30 days of moving in. Residences must comply with local building codes. Subsection numbers beyond (c)(8) to be pinned from the official text.

citations.title: Geographic Location of Community-Integrated Living Arrangements
citations.requirement: Siting rules for HCBS settings. New provider-owned or controlled sites may not be adjacent to, across from, diagonal to or behind another waiver-funded residential or day site of the same provider unless a waiver is granted. They may not be in a building that provides inpatient institutional treatment. No more than 25% of units in a building may be Department-funded CILAs owned or controlled by CILA providers. Waiver requests are filed before leasing, buying or taking possession.

citations.title: Administrative Requirements
citations.requirement: (a) Corporate, association or local-government providers have a governing body with authority over operations. Providers must have a way to get input from individuals, guardians and representatives to the governing body. (b) Employees are licensed or certified as Illinois law requires. The agency may not employ anyone (including contractors, volunteers and practitioners) until it has checked the DPH Health Care Worker Registry and the DCFS State Central Register/CANTS. It must also have received the results of the applicable registry or list, and the inquiry may not occur more than 30 calendar days before the first day of employment. Checks are repeated on a schedule that completes them every 365 days. The agency complies with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act. (d) DSPs and anyone with direct care responsibility demonstrate competence in the listed training areas (A)-(M) as part of orientation, with enough trained staff to cover absences. (e) Volunteer training applies. The section also requires the agency to notify the individual's guardian or parent of an abuse/neglect allegation within 24 hours of receiving it. Each agency must have and use a process for reporting and handling complaints. Exact paragraph letters to be pinned.

citations.title: Application for Waiver of the Prohibition Against Employment
citations.requirement: Provides the process for applying for a waiver of the prohibition against employment (Health Care Worker Background Check Act). Only the section title was retrieved; pull the text before writing the procedure.

citations.title: Monitoring and Evaluation
citations.requirement: Agency monitoring and evaluation obligations. Only the section title was retrieved; pull the text before writing the QI procedure.

citations.title: Monitors and Receiverships
citations.requirement: New section in the 2024 Rule 115 amendments. Substantive triggers and roles come from the 115.120 definitions of Independent Monitor and Receiver. The section text itself was not retrieved.

citations.title: License Application
citations.requirement: New-provider requirements must be completed within one year of requesting an application. The application certifies compliance with Section 4 of the Act, the Confidentiality Act, Part 115, 59 Ill. Adm. Code 120 and 42 CFR 441.301(c)(1)-(4). Settings must not be of the type in 42 CFR 441.301(c)(5)(v), and provider-owned or controlled sites must meet (c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E). The application requires agency policies and procedures, an organizational chart, staffing patterns and staff qualifications. The nonrefundable fee follows Section 4(d) of the Act. The renewal application is due at least 120 days before expiration after Department notice. BALC and DDD must be notified of any ownership change within 60 business days. The agency must be operational within 18 months or the application is treated as abandoned.

citations.title: 24-Hour Service
citations.requirement: 24-hour service requirement. It sits in Subpart E (Host Family Living Arrangements), so cite it only for host family settings. For shift-staff homes rely on the continuous supervision definition in 115.120 and the Personal Plan/Implementation Strategy.

citations.title: Definitions (abuse, neglect, financial exploitation) - OIG Rule 50
citations.requirement: 115.120 adopts the Part 50.10 definitions of abuse and financial exploitation, and critical incidents include abuse, neglect and exploitation as defined in Part 50. Only the incorporation by reference was verified, not the Part 50 text itself. Reporting steps and timelines in Part 50 were NOT retrieved.

citations.title: Referenced in 115.240 (medication administration)
citations.requirement: 115.240 requires certification that medications are provided or supervised in line with the Administrative Act and Part 116. The Part 116 title and text were NOT retrieved; confirm the title and requirements before citing.

citations.title: Person-Centered Planning
citations.requirement: HCBS waiver participants, guardians, ISC agencies and provider agencies comply with person-centered planning requirements. Providers develop an Implementation Strategy within 20 calendar days of signing the Personal Plan.

citations.title: Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act
citations.requirement: Governs confidentiality of records and communications. Rule 115 requires agencies to certify compliance, and informed consent includes consent for releases of information. Act text was not retrieved; only its incorporation by Part 115.

citations.title: Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Code - rights
citations.requirement: 115.250 requires individual rights to be protected under Chapter II of the Code, except that seclusion is not permitted.

citations.title: Health Care Worker Background Check Act
citations.requirement: Part 115 implements this Act (per its authority note), and 115.320(b) requires compliance. The Act text was not retrieved.

citations.title: Authorized Electronic Monitoring in Community-Integrated Living Arrangements and Developmental Disability Facilities Act
citations.requirement: 115.120 defines authorized electronic monitoring and electronic monitoring devices by reference to this Act. Monitoring is placement of a device in an individual's room under the Act. Act text was not retrieved.

citations.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance - Steps for CILA
citations.title: New Provider Guidance - Steps for CILA
citations.requirement: Criminal background check before hire and annually. Illinois State Police fingerprint check reported to the Health Care Worker Registry. Staff trained as DSP (DD Aide) or completing training before working alone, with completion reported to HCWR. Anyone giving direct care more than 20% of the time is trained as a DSP. First aid/CPR and OIG Rule 50 abuse/neglect training renew every two years. RN with unencumbered Illinois license who completes DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars. BALC unannounced visit within one year of first admission, site visit within six months, then permanent license.

citations.title: Contents of request for a waiver - person-centered planning and HCBS settings
citations.requirement: Rule 115.410(a)(2) requires CILAs serving waiver participants to meet person-centered planning and settings requirements in (c)(1)-(4). Settings may not be of the type in (c)(5)(v), and provider-owned or controlled sites must meet (c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E).

citations.cite: Medicaid HCBS Waiver for Adults with Developmental Disabilities (IL.0350.R05.04)
citations.title: 1915(c) waiver in effect January 1, 2026
citations.requirement: Waiver under which CILA services are paid. HFS is the Medicaid agency and IDHS-DDD is the operating agency.

citations.title: Person-Centered Planning Process - IDHS
citations.requirement: Provider signature page is due back to the ISC within 10 calendar days of receiving the Personal Plan. The Implementation Strategy is due within 20 calendar days of the QIDP signing the Provider Signature Page.

citations.cite: IDHS Person Centered Planning Policy and Guidelines for DD Waiver Services
citations.title: Person Centered Planning Policy and Guidelines
citations.requirement: Providers give the individual/guardian and ISC a copy of the Implementation Strategy. The individual or guardian signs it, and the guidance says the ISC does not sign or approve it. Providers must make sure all billed services are identified in the Personal Plan and tell the ISC if a service change is needed.

citations.cite: IDHS DDD Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) Policy
citations.title: Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) Policy
citations.requirement: EVV for IMPACT-enrolled providers billing personal care or home health care services. From April 1, 2026, providers must keep quarterly EVV compliance above 75%. Whether 60D/61H CILA claims are covered is unverified; confirm with DDD.

citations.title: IMPACT Provider Enrollment
citations.requirement: IMPACT is the Medicaid enrollment and reimbursement system. Enrollment must be completed before federal reimbursement.

citations.title: January 1, 2024 Wage/Rate Increase
citations.requirement: CILA provider agencies certify that wage increases are passed through to direct care staff.

citations.cite: IDHS Independent Service Coordination (ISC) Manual, Section 8.2
citations.title: Person Centered Planning - The Discovery Process
citations.requirement: The ISC has 30 calendar days after the person begins DDD Waiver services to complete Discovery and develop the Personal Plan. The ISC submits the Crisis Transition Plan and Funding Request for people in crisis (homelessness, abuse or neglect).

citations.title: Standards and Licensure Requirements for Community-Integrated Living Arrangements
citations.requirement: Part-level cite, used where a rule paragraph was seen but its exact section/subsection was not confirmed. That includes the required record contents (written informed consent to participate, prior service history, Personal Plan), admission policies in writing, life-safety compliance, current Personal Plans/Implementation Strategies kept at the residence, and surveys at renewal and for complaints. Pin the exact section from the official text before finalizing. Amended effective 5/31/2023 (47 Ill. Reg. 8485).

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Authorized CILA Agency Representative Responsibilities
state_specifics: Corporate, association or local-government providers need a governing body with authority over the agency and all its programs, services, facilities and residences (115.320(a)(1)).
Provide a way for individuals, guardians and representatives to give input to the governing body (115.320(a)(2)).

The governing body appoints the Authorized CILA Agency Representative, who has overall fiscal and programmatic responsibility (115.120). That person signs and dates the license and renewal applications (115.410(a)(4)).
Keep an organizational chart, staffing patterns and staff qualifications (submitted with the application, 115.410(a)(3)(E)).
Maximum 8 individuals per CILA site.
Rule 115 contains no licensure staff ratio. Staffing is driven by Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies.

policies.title: Licensure, Site Certification and Provider Agreements (BALC / DDD)
state_specifics: BALC licenses the agency and certifies each site. BALC contact: 401 S. Clinton, 7th Floor, Chicago, IL 60607; 312-814-5310; DHS.BALC@illinois.gov (confirm email spelling).
Application fee is $200 and nonrefundable (statutory cap per 210 ILCS 135/4).
Renewal application is due at least 120 days before the license expires, after Department notice (115.410(c)).
Notify BALC and DDD within 60 business days of any ownership change (115.410(d)).
The agency must be operational within 18 months or the process is treated as abandoned (115.410(e)).

Provisional license is for up to one year, one site, up to 8 people. BALC inspects a new site before occupancy, within 15 working days of receiving fire clearances and documents. BALC makes an unannounced visit within a year of first admission and a site visit within six months, and a passing agency gets a 3-year permanent license. HB5471 would shorten the term and its status is unverified.
DDD enrollment steps wait for BALC's provisional license notice. IMPACT enrollment is required before Medicaid reimbursement.
Proximity limits and the 25% building cap (115.310) apply to every new site. File any proximity waiver before leasing, buying or taking possession.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Policies and procedures are part of the license application (115.410(a)(3)(D)). Failing the BALC policy review bars reapplying for one calendar year (IDHS New Provider Guidance).
Review the disaster preparedness plan at least annually and revise as needed (115.300(c)(8)).
Keep admission policies in writing and available for review.
Keep a copy of the restraint policy (115.245).
Reflect the amended Part 115 effective 5/31/2023, including person-centered planning and conflict-free case management. Do not rely on older BALC templates.
Keep a version log with approver, date and next review date.

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
state_specifics: Follow the monitoring and evaluation requirements of 115.325 (text to be pinned).

Review at least quarterly: critical incidents (including CIRAS entries), injuries, peer-to-peer aggression, restraint use, unscheduled hospitalizations, missing-person events, rights complaints and survey findings.
Every death gets an internal mortality review. Deaths are critical incidents (115.120). No Part 115 mortality-review procedure was located, so this is agency practice.
Refer restraint use and behavior modifications to the Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee (115.245).
Document corrective actions and track them to closure. Keep deficiency corrections available for BALC/DDD.

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing and Service Documentation
state_specifics: CILA services are paid under waiver IL.0350.R05.04 (HFS Medicaid agency, IDHS-DDD operating agency) through IMPACT. Bill only services identified in the individual's Personal Plan.
CILA rates are individually determined (program codes 60D for 24-hour/host family, 61H for intermittent). Get each person's rate letter before admission.
The CILA rate does not include day program costs. Day programs are billed separately (115.200).
Documentation must support each billed day and show services delivered per the Implementation Strategy.

EVV: required for IMPACT providers billing personal care or home health care. Whether 60D/61H claims are covered is unverified, so ask DDD in writing. If covered, quarterly compliance must stay above 75% from 4/1/2026.
Keep the wage pass-through certification and payroll records for each DDD rate increase.
Medicaid does not pay room and board, so residents pay it from income such as SSI.

policies.title: Agency Closure, Independent Monitors and Receiverships
state_specifics: The Department may assign an Independent Monitor (not Department or State staff) when the agency operates without a license or the license is suspended, revoked or not renewed. Other triggers: notice to end or not renew the DDD agreement, a closure without adequate transition arrangements at least 30 days beforehand, an emergency threat to health or safety the agency cannot or will not fix, or termination from Medicaid (115.120).
A court-appointed Receiver takes custody of an unlicensed or sanctioned agency and cannot be an owner or affiliate (115.120).
Closure plan: notify BALC/DDD, ISC agencies, individuals and guardians; arrange transition at least 30 days before closure; transfer records under the Confidentiality Act.
Cooperate with monitors, who observe operations, advise on compliance and report to the Department.
Section 115.326 text was not retrieved; pull it before finalizing.

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
state_specifics: Share and explain the current Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201) with the individual and guardian at entry and annually. Document that it was done.
Rights follow Chapter II of the Mental Health and DD Code. Seclusion is not permitted.
Right to remain in the CILA unless the person voluntarily withdraws or meets the 115.215 termination criteria.

Right to contact GAC, Equip for Equality, the DHS OIG, the Department and the agency human rights committee. Staff offer help and give each person the address and telephone number of GAC, OIG, the Department and Equip for Equality (confirm current numbers before posting).
Right to choose private physicians and professionals, documented in the plan.

The setting supports community integration, control of personal resources, privacy, dignity and respect, and freedom from coercion. It must not be an institutional-type setting (441.301(c)(5)(v)). Provider-owned or controlled sites meet 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E): residency agreement, privacy and lockable bedroom doors, control of schedule and access to food, visitors at any time, and physical accessibility.

policies.title: Rights Restrictions, Modifications and Due Process
state_specifics: Restrictions are allowed only as an individualized modification in the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy. The strategy states periods of time and activity restrictions at home and the locations and time frames for community access (115.230).
Include an assurance that interventions and supports will cause no harm.
Restrictive behavior supports need Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee approval (115.245).
Restrictions may not be used for staff convenience or staffing concerns (115.230).
Seclusion, time-out and aversive procedures are prohibited (115.250).
Document informed consent from the individual or guardian, review the restriction on a set schedule, and give the individual a way to contest it (grievance, ISC, GAC/Equip for Equality).

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Each agency must have and use a process for reporting and handling complaints in addition to the abuse/neglect/exploitation process (115.320).
Give individuals and guardians the contact details for GAC, OIG, DHS and Equip for Equality (115.250).
Provide for individual/guardian input to the governing body (115.320(a)(2)).
Written procedure: how to file (oral or written, with staff help), who investigates, response timeframe (agency-set), written outcome, and no retaliation.
Complaints alleging abuse, neglect or exploitation go through BSP-03 instead.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: The Mental Health and DD Confidentiality Act (740 ILCS 110) governs records. Informed consent covers releases of information (115.120). Rule 115 requires certification of compliance with the Act (115.410).
Publish and give a notice of privacy practices. Keep a release log and disclosure accounting.
Breach notification procedure under the HIPAA Breach Notification Rule.
Respect each person's privacy in bedroom and bath. Electronic monitoring only under 210 ILCS 165 (see IR-09).
Staff confidentiality agreement at hire. Records stored securely; electronic records allowed for Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies kept at the residence.

policies.title: Personal Funds, Personal Resources and Property
state_specifics: Individuals must be able to control their personal resources (115.200; 115.120 community integration).
Financial exploitation is defined in Part 50 and is a critical incident (115.120).
Keep a separate account or ledger per individual with no commingling. Reconcile monthly, with receipts and two-person count for cash.
Use a written room-and-board agreement. Medicaid does not pay room and board, and residents typically pay from income such as SSI. Confirm any permitted charge with DDD/BALC.
If the agency is a representative payee, follow SSA duties on use of benefits and annual accounting.
Inventory personal property and replace or reimburse for loss or damage caused by staff.
No staff borrowing, gifts or personal transactions with individuals.

policies.title: Informed Consent, Guardianship and Decision-Making Support
state_specifics: Informed consent means permission freely given after full disclosure of benefits and liabilities, including releases of information (115.120).
Written informed consent to participate in a CILA is obtained and documented in the record (115.200).

Guardian means the court-appointed plenary or limited guardian. A limited guardian's authority is only as the order allows (115.120). A guardian never serves as the individual's host family caregiver (host family rule).
Coercion is defined and prohibited (115.120).
Support individuals to make their own decisions in the planning process.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
state_specifics: No otherwise qualified individual may be denied placement solely on diagnosis (115.210).
Communal areas must meet ADA standards. Sites must have capacity for wheelchair or mobility device users before placement is offered (115.200).
Provide interpreters, translated rights materials and accessible formats at no cost.
Reasonable accommodation requests are logged and answered in writing.
Admission decisions are based on the person's needs and the home's capacity, not on discriminatory factors.

policies.title: Sexual Health, Relationships and Consent
state_specifics: Support each individual's right to sexual health and healthy sexual practices and to be free from sexual exploitation and abuse (115.220).
The individual is assessed on decision-making capacity to give consent to sexual activity (115.220).
Sexual abuse allegations go through BSP-03/BSP-04.
Guidance for staff on privacy, education and boundaries; document supports in the Implementation Strategy.

policies.title: Authorized Electronic Monitoring in Individual Bedrooms
state_specifics: Authorized electronic monitoring is placement of a device in an individual's room under the Authorized Electronic Monitoring in CILAs and DD Facilities Act (210 ILCS 165) (115.120).
Cover who may request monitoring, consent and notice, roommate consent, and posting. Pull the Act's text before writing the procedure, as it was not retrieved.
Agency-installed cameras or recording in bedrooms or baths outside the Act are prohibited. Monitoring is never a substitute for required staffing or supervision.
Footage is handled as confidential record information.

policies.title: Referral, Admission and Transition In
state_specifics: Eligibility: at least 18 with a developmental disability and need for CILA services. Age waiver may be requested for 17.5 to under 18 (115.210). No denial solely on diagnosis. Written admission policies available for review.

Referrals come through the ISC agency. The ISC completes Discovery and the Personal Plan within 30 calendar days after waiver services start. The provider signature page is due to the ISC within 10 calendar days of receiving the Personal Plan.

At entry: obtain written informed consent, prior service history and the Personal Plan (Part 115 record requirements). Share and explain the Rights form (IL 462-1201), and offer a residency agreement for provider-owned sites. Document that rights were explained.
The individual or guardian actively participates in choosing the CILA and a home from those available to the general public (115.200).

Confirm the site is certified and accessible before offering placement. Train new individuals within 30 days of move-in on fire, severe weather, missing persons, emergencies, poison control and death (115.300).
Obtain the individual's rate letter before accepting an admission. Crisis admissions (homelessness, abuse, neglect) go through the ISC crisis process.

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning, Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy
state_specifics: The ISC develops the Personal Plan. The agency's QIDP signs the Provider Signature Page and the agency writes the Implementation Strategy on Form IL462-4470 within 20 calendar days of that signature.

The strategy covers only the Personal Plan areas the agency agreed to support. It is signed by the individual and guardian. The 115.120 definition lists the ISC as a signer, but DDD guidance says the ISC does not sign or approve it. Confirm current practice with BALC/DDD.
Give copies of the strategy and updates to the individual and guardian (and ISC). It becomes part of the record, and current copies are kept at the residence.
The QIDP reviews the strategy at least monthly and documents the review. Update at least annually or on change of status or request.
The QIDP convenes the Provider Support Team (QIDP, DSP, nurse/other professionals as needed) with the individual, guardian and an ISC representative.
Bill only for services identified in the Personal Plan. Notify the ISC when a service change is needed.

policies.title: Assessments, Health Risk Screening and Requests for Additional Supports
state_specifics: Assess each individual on entry and at least annually. Health screening uses the Department's web-based tool, with a paper request allowed with justification (confirm the subsection in 115.225).
Identified risks must appear in the Implementation Strategy.
The team may request additional staff resources or supports. The Department responds within ten business days of receipt (115.214).
Non-base support hours are professionally reassessed at least annually and results reported to the Department (115.214).
For intermittent supports, the ISC and CILA agency submit a CILA rate determination packet to the Department (115.230).

policies.title: Implementation of Supports and Daily Documentation
state_specifics: Provide care and supervision based on assessed needs, and be available 24 hours (115.220).
Document daily support delivered against each Implementation Strategy outcome. Notes are dated and signed.
Document the QIDP monthly review. Record contents must include consent, prior service history, Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy (Part 115 record rules).
Report changes in functional status to the QIDP, who updates the strategy.
Keep current copies of Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies at the residence (digital or paper).

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
state_specifics: Community integration means opportunities to seek competitive integrated employment, engage in community life, and control personal resources (115.120).

Support time out of the home in non-disability-specific activities of the person's choice, such as worship, recreation, education, library, shopping and holidays. Support communication by phone, electronic media and mail, and vacations.
Day program authorizations are billed separately from the CILA rate (115.200). Staff must still cover the home when individuals miss day programming.
Offer employment exploration at least annually through the ISC planning process. Record choices in the Personal Plan.
Support relationships with non-paid community members (115.220).

policies.title: Time Alone and Independent Community Access
state_specifics: Someone needing continuous supervision may stay alone or go into the community independently only under specific circumstances (115.230).
The provider support team assesses ability and desire. The decision is based on need and preference, not staff convenience.
The Implementation Strategy states times, locations and time frames. Continuous supervision ranges from line of sight to present and accessible, as the strategy specifies (115.120).
Include an emergency plan and a way for the person to reach staff.

policies.title: Respite Services (if offered)
state_specifics: Before respite, require a physician statement that the individual has no contagious disease (115.205).
Document that the respite guest will not jeopardize the health and safety of other residents.
Respite lasting more than two weeks requires Department approval before the first two weeks end, and only in emergencies.
Adopt this policy only if the agency will offer respite; otherwise note it as not offered.

policies.title: Transition, Discharge and Termination of Services
state_specifics: Individuals may remain in the CILA unless they voluntarily withdraw or meet the 115.215 criteria (115.250). Pull the 115.215 criteria and procedure verbatim before finalizing.
Termination is never a punitive response to behavior or a way to avoid staffing needs. Coordinate with the ISC, QIDP, individual and guardian, and document the team recommendation.
Give the person and guardian written notice and the rights/contact information for GAC, OIG and Equip for Equality (115.250).
Transfer records only with a signed release (Confidentiality Act). Plan the transition and follow up after the move.
Agency closure is handled under GOV-06.

policies.title: Medication Administration and Staff Certification
state_specifics: A licensed physician (MD/DO) is responsible for medical services including prescribing (115.240).

A physician examines the individual before psychotropics start. AIMS screening at least every six months for individuals on psychotropics. Physician reviews medications and sees the individual at least every six months (115.240).
Medications are provided or supervised under the Administrative Act and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116 (Part 116 text to be pinned).
Staff help individuals access medication information, including observing and reporting effects and side effects (115.220).
Staff certification: confirm the current DHS-approved medication administration course and passing score with BALC before staff administer. Older hour counts were from an outdated BALC document.
Use an MAR, error/incident reporting to the RN and QIDP, secure storage and a controlled-substance count.

policies.title: Nursing Oversight and Health Care Coordination
state_specifics: The agency must have an RN with an unencumbered Illinois license who completes the DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars (IDHS New Provider Guidance). Verify the license on the IDFPR site before hire.
A nurse is part of the Provider Support Team when necessary (115.220). DSPs work under QIDP, nurse or other authorized higher-level supervision (115.120).
The RN trains and oversees medication staff, reviews health risk screening, and coordinates physician visits (at least every six months, 115.240).
The agency is licensed or certified as required by Illinois law for health professionals (115.320(b)(1)).

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
state_specifics: Health risks identified in screening and the Personal Plan must be addressed in the Implementation Strategy (115.120 Implementation Strategy; PCS-03).
Write individual seizure, choking, dysphagia and aspiration protocols from the RN and physician orders, and train all staff on them before working alone.
Staff keep first aid/CPR current and renew every two years (IDHS New Provider Guidance).
Document vital signs, weights and medical appointments, and share health information with the ISC and physician as the plan requires.

policies.title: Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care
state_specifics: Medical emergencies, unscheduled hospitalizations, injuries of known or unknown origin and law enforcement or fire department involvement are critical incidents (115.120) and are reported through CIRAS.
Staff and individuals must know how to respond to medical and psychiatric emergencies and poison control (115.300(c)(8)).
Post an accessible telephone with the site number and nearest poison control center (115.300(c)(8)(F)).
Call 911 first for life-threatening events, then notify the RN, QIDP, guardian and ISC. Send a face sheet, medication list and Personal Plan summary with the person.
Record the change of condition and update the Implementation Strategy.

policies.title: Death of an Individual
state_specifics: Deaths are critical incidents. Deaths reportable under Part 50 go to the OIG, and those not otherwise reportable still go through the critical incident process (115.120).
Staff are trained on responding to a death (115.300(c)(8)(C)).

Procedure: emergency response, 911 and law enforcement/coroner as required, immediate notice to guardian/next of kin, ISC, QIDP and administrator, and incident entry in CIRAS. Preserve records and the scene.
Do not release belongings or funds except under written authorization and law. Follow IR-05 for funds.
